thread:
Clara: Quick sync — I'm weighing a prefetching proxy at the edge vs an internal agent for telemetry enrichment and billing-key resolution. Need tradeoffs on latency, cost, and attribution fidelity.
Mike: Proxy wins for consolidated tenant resolution and cross-request batching. Fewer lookups overall -> lower egress cost.
Thao: Agent keeps context local which helps span continuity. If sampling decisions or small in-process caches matter, agent beats a proxy for tail variance.
Ravi: Big gotcha is dedupe/idempotency. If proxy does prefetch and adds billing keys, we must sign or version them so retries don't reassign cost.
Jen: Also think about observability backpressure. Proxy can queue & drop gracefully, but then we hide source-level failures. Agent makes failures visible per host.
Clara: Example of simple proxy config we sketched this morning:
```
route: POST /ingest
prefetch: /resolve-tenant?svc=headers.x-client
cache_ttl: 45s
passthrough_on_miss: true
```
Mike: That TTL amortizes lookups well for bursty traffic. But be careful with long-lived connections to KV stores — we saw correlation with increased tail latencies in dev.
Thao: From a schema perspective: proxy must not mutate span ids or drop provenance headers. We need an immutable envelope field (redwood.infer.orig_headers) to preserve original trace metadata.
Ravi: For cost attribution we need deterministic binding. If proxy resolves tenant -> attach billing_key and a resolution_digest. If agent resolves, include resolver_instance_id so we can map counts back for chargeback.
Jen: Sampling interplay: proxy-level sampling skews downstream counters unless we propagate a sample_decision marker so downstream can reconstruct denominators.
ops-bot: FYI: staging infra has 2 spare t3 proxies for canary routing if you want to test.
Clara: Proposal: Build a hybrid experiment — proxy-first with passthrough toggle. Measure: (1) 95/99 tail latency delta, (2) billing resolution lookup QPS & egress, (3) attribution mismatch rate against gold-set prompts. Two-week AB.
Mike: Add one more metric: enrichment cache miss-to-hit ratio per tenant and the percent of requests that change billing_key on retry.
Thao: Also plan for a migration hook: a reconciliation job that compares proxy-assigned billing_key vs agent-resolved for a sample set and emits anomalies to a paging channel.
Ravi: Implementation notes: make resolved keys HMACed (short digest) and include resolver version so we can rotate algorithms without losing lineage.
Jen: UX note — Console should surface which path served the request (proxy/agent) and a small latency waterfall. That made triage much faster in the prefix-cache rollout.
Clara: Ok — I'll draft a tiny RFC with the experiment matrix and rollouts (canary->regional->global). Assigning owners: Mike on proxy perf, Thao on schema contract, Ravi on reconciliation, Jen on observability dashboards.
Mike: :thumbsup: I'll stub the proxy config and a lightweight harness that flips passthrough via header.
Thao: Will draft schema additions (immutable envelope + sample_decision flag).
Ravi: I'll scope the reconciliation job and HMAC scheme.
Jen: I'll mock the dashboard widgets and the alerting rules for attribution drift.
Clara: Thanks all — circling back next Tue after initial measurement plan is in the draft.
ops-bot: Note: created ticket INF-8421 to track the hybrid prefetch experiment and owners.
